article_title: Transgender migrant’s reported 6-month plea deal for child rape sparks fury
article_content:
A Colombian national who officials have said entered the United States illegally in 2023 is expected to receive a six-month sentence, time that has already been served, after pleading guilty to raping a 14-year-old boy in a Manhattan bodega bathroom.
Nicol Alexandra Contreras-Suarez, 31, a transgender woman, pleaded guilty to second-degree rape in New York Supreme Court for sexually assaulting a teenager in East Harlem in 2025, according to The New York Post.
Newsweek contacted the Manhattan District Attormey's Office and Justice Department via email outside of normal office hours on Wednesday.
ICE lodged an immigration detainer, a step which can precede transfer to federal custody in removal proceedings, with Manhattan Central Booking on February 13, DHS said in a July 2025 press release detailing Contreras-Suarez's case.
New York City is a sanctuary jurisdiction that limits cooperation between local law enforcement and federal immigration authorities in certain cases
The reported plea deal has ellicited strong responses on social media in a case that has intensified debate over immigration enforcement and local-federal cooperation.
What To Know
Contreras-Suarez previously faced charges for first-degree rape of a child less than 17 and stalking, according to a July 2025 news release from the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).
Prosecutors said the new plea deal, which spares the victim testifying, was agreed in consultation with the victim’s family, the Post reported.
“We expect the defendant to remain detained and be deported following sentencing, due to the felony conviction,” a spokesperson for the Manhattan District Attorney’s Office told the newspaper.
Contreras-Suarez has been held in custody at Rikers Island in New York since legal proceedings began in July 2025.
Customs and Border Protection (CBP) arrested Contreras‑Suarez in March 2023 for illegally entering the United States at San Ysidro, California, and was later released, according to the DHS' July 2025 release.
On February 13, 2025, ICE placed an immigration detainer on Contreras-Suarez with Manhattan Central Booking. An immigration detainer is a request from federal authorities asking local law enforcement to hold a person in custody so ICE can take them into federal custody ahead of removal from the country.
In December 2025, DHS said in a news release that 7,113 individuals without legal status are currently in custody across New York jurisdictions with active immigration detainers.
Trump officials and Republican lawmakers have argued that sanctuary policies, such as in New York, can hinder federal enforcement efforts and pose public safety concerns, while Democrats and progressive advocates say the measures are intended to build trust between immigrant communities and police.
What People Are Saying
U.S. Representative Andy Ogles, the Republican of Tennessee, responded on X: "I’m beyond angry!"
Fox News commentator Guy Benson wrote on X, "Being in two Special Protected Identity Classes in a left-wing jurisdiction sure has its benefits, like allowances to do crimes with little to no accountability. “Progress”!
Right wing social media channel Libs of TikTok wrote on X, "This foreign child r*pist needs to be DEPORTED IMMEDIATELY. Do not release him back onto the streets."
“This creep should’ve never been released into our country,” then-DHS spokeperson Tricia McLaughlin said in a July 2025 news release on the case. “Thanks to the failed sanctuary policies and Biden’s open-border agenda, this serial criminal was freed to prey on innocent American children – but that ends now. ICE will not allow predators like Contreras-Suarez to terrorize American citizens.”
What Happens Next
Contreras-Suarez's sentencing hearing is scheduled to take please on April 27, the New York Post reports.
